overview: Server-side anticheats treat the join-game packet as the state anchor of a play session. It carries no movement or combat data, so no check flags it; instead the packet re-reads the player model (entity id, gamemode, dimension, world name) in modern simulation anticheats, while classic anticheats watch the login events that surround the join. The security-relevant detail is what the packet resets: any anticheat that keeps per-player state must re-arm it here or every later check inherits stale data.

checks.name: Join-game state reset (Grim)
checks.purpose: Re-sync the simulated player model to the join-game payload: entity id, gamemode, dimension, world name and the death-screen flag.
checks.how_it_works: PacketPlayerRespawn listens on PacketSendEvent with HIGH priority. The JOIN_GAME branch wraps the packet as WrapperPlayServerJoinGame, copies entityId, gamemode, dimensionType and worldName into the GrimPlayer, sets showsDeathScreen from isRespawnScreenEnabled on 1.15+ clients, and re-arms the compensated world dimension on 1.17+ servers. The same listener owns the respawn and update-health branches, so this file is the single state-reset point for the whole session lifecycle.
checks.detects: Nothing directly: it prevents desync between the server's world state and the movement simulation, which is the precondition for every later check. A player model that never received its join payload would false-flag reach, fly and velocity checks.
checks.variations: Shard's PacketListener routes JOIN_GAME into handleJoinGame, which stores the entity id and gamemode and clears the compensated entity list. Artemis registers GPacketPlayServerLogin in its packet repository (SERVER_PLAY + 40) and fires LoginCallback on login success. Daedalus starts a 60-tick lastLogin timer used to exempt movement checks after join.

checks.name: Join-game handling (Shard)
checks.purpose: Initialize the per-player packet state when the play session starts: entity id, gamemode and a clean compensated entity list.
checks.how_it_works: PacketListener.onPacketSend switches on Play.Server packet types. JOIN_GAME is wrapped as WrapperPlayServerJoinGame and passed to handleJoinGame, which stores the entity id and gamemode on the ShardPlayer and clears compensatedEntities. The same dispatch routes RESPAWN, the SPAWN_* family and DESTROY_ENTITIES, so the join handler is one branch of the packet-state machine that all simulation checks consume.
checks.detects: Nothing by itself. It guarantees the entity id used by the client-side self entity matches the server's, which every movement and combat check assumes.
checks.variations: Grim does the same job inside PacketPlayerRespawn; Hydro resets state from the login-success packet instead (PacketEventsJoinQuitListener). Shard also records login timestamps into its violation database (recordLogin) for session analytics.

checks.name: Logins (NoCheatPlus)
checks.purpose: Rate-limit simultaneous logins to blunt login-flood spam bots that join and disconnect repeatedly.
checks.how_it_works: A CHAT_LOGINS check driven by ChatListener.onPlayerLogin. It buckets login timestamps into a six-slot ActionFrequency ring per world (or globally when per-world counting is off), scores the bucket sum against cc.loginsLimit and cancels the login when the rate exceeds it. The join-game packet itself is never parsed; the check keys off the Bukkit PlayerLoginEvent that fires around the join handshake, which is how 1.8-generation anticheats watch the join domain without touching packet code.
checks.detects: Login spam and mass-bot joins; the paired Relog check adds per-player relog throttling with a configurable deny list.
checks.variations: Negativity and BetterAnticheat (Velocity) do the same on PostLoginEvent; Artemis runs LoginCallback after login success; Daedalus and NCP both keep a per-player login timestamp used by movement exemptions, which is the other common join-domain pattern.
